$$f(x) = x^3 - x^2 - 3x + 1$$
$$f(0) = 1 ;; f(1) = -2$$
Does the Intermediate Value Theorem promise a zero in $(0, 1)$?
questions.explain: 0 is between them, and $f$ is continuous.

questions.text:
$$f(x) = x^2 - 2$$
$$f(1) = -1 ;; f(2) = 2$$
Does the Intermediate Value Theorem promise a zero in $(1, 2)$?
questions.explain: 0 is between them, and $f$ is continuous.

questions.text:
$$f(x) = x^2 + 1$$
$$f(-1) = 2 ;; f(1) = 2$$
Does the Intermediate Value Theorem promise a zero in $(-1, 1)$?
questions.explain: Both values have the same sign, so the IVT promises nothing.

questions.text:
$$f(x) = cos(x) - x$$
$$f(0) = 1 ;; f(1) = -0.459698$$
Does the Intermediate Value Theorem promise a zero in $(0, 1)$?
questions.explain: 0 is between them, and $f$ is continuous.

questions.text:
$$f(x) = x^3 + x + 1$$
$$f(-1) = -1 ;; f(0) = 1$$
Does the Intermediate Value Theorem promise a zero in $(-1, 0)$?
questions.explain: 0 is between them, and $f$ is continuous.

questions.text:

questions.explain: Both values have the same sign, so the IVT promises nothing.
